answers.power_state: Lights/fan turn on but no display

free_text: laptop turns on but black screen, fan spins

diagnosis.primary_fault: Black Screen / RAM Contact Oxidation / Loose Display Cable
supporting_evidence: Reported symptoms directly match indicator terms: lights/fan turn on but no display, black screen, no display
Strong symptom co-occurrence pattern identified: [lights + no display, fan + no display]
safe_checks: 1. Connect the laptop to an external TV or monitor via HDMI.
2. If external monitor displays the desktop normally, the motherboard and GPU are fine; the issue is internal panel, cable, or backlight.
3. Check Caps Lock / Num Lock: if the light toggles on and off when pressed, the OS is booting properly behind the dark screen.
4. Shine a bright flashlight at an angle at the dark screen: if faint desktop icons are visible, the panel backlight or fuse has failed.
advanced_steps: 1. Power off, open bottom chassis, and disconnect the battery cable from the motherboard.
2. Unclip the RAM modules and remove them.
3. Rub the golden contact pins on both sides of each RAM stick with a clean pencil eraser to remove microscopic oxidation.
4. Reinsert RAM firmly into the slots at a 30-degree angle and click down. Reconnect battery and test boot.
safety_instructions: Disconnect the battery before touching RAM slots or the display eDP cable. Shorting display pins can burn the motherboard backlight fuse!
troubleshooting_steps: 1. Connect the laptop to an external TV or monitor via HDMI.
2. If external monitor displays the desktop normally, the motherboard and GPU are fine; the issue is internal panel, cable, or backlight.
3. Check Caps Lock / Num Lock: if the light toggles on and off when pressed, the OS is booting properly behind the dark screen.
4. Shine a bright flashlight at an angle at the dark screen: if faint desktop icons are visible, the panel backlight or fuse has failed.

2. Unclip the RAM modules and remove them.

repair_recommendation.rationale: Reseating RAM sticks with an eraser or reconnecting the eDP display cable fixes 80% of 'power on with black screen' problems.
